title: Maths reference: Year 7 Statistics
summary: The words and methods from Year 7 Statistics, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/statistics-7 (see snippets/maths-algebra-7.json for the format; split from the strand courses' card files on 1 Nov 2026).

items.label: discrete and continuous
items.hint: Discrete data takes separate values (number of siblings). Continuous data can be any value in a range (height, time), and is rounded when recorded.

items.label: mean
items.hint: Add the values, then share equally. An outlier pulls the mean towards it.
items.board:
widget: data
values: 3, 5, 5, 6, 11
range: 0, 15
show: mean, median

items.label: median
items.hint: Sort first; the middle value, or halfway between the two middle values for an even count.

items.label: mode and range
items.hint: There can be two modes, or none. The range is a simple measure of spread.

items.label: choosing a measure
items.hint: With an outlier, the median describes a typical value better than the mean. Without, the mean uses every value. For 'most common', use the mode.

items.label: stem-and-leaf plot
items.hint: Tens as stems, units as leaves in order; include every stem, even with no leaves; give a key.
items.board:
widget: data
values: 23, 31, 35, 35, 38, 42, 47, 51
view: stem
show: none
items.shows: Stems are the tens, leaves the units

items.label: comparing data sets
items.hint: Describe shape (symmetrical or skewed, clusters, gaps, outliers), centre and spread. Compare both centre and spread, with numbers, in context.
items.board:
widget: data
values: 12, 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 18
second: 6, 10, 13, 16, 19, 20, 22
names: Class A, Class B
range: 0, 25
show: median, range
items.shows: Similar medians; Class B much more spread

items.label: statistical investigation
items.hint: Ask a question data can answer, plan the variable and a fair sample, collect and display the data, describe its shape, centre and spread, then report the answer with its limits.
